ai.description: The Tonkin Huia Frog reaches 4–6 cm. It is olive-green to brown with dark mottling and a distinct, pointed snout. It features long, slender limbs and prominent, expanded toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Odorrana nasica* is best distinguished by its exceptionally long, pointed snout and a distinct, fleshy rostral appendage that overhangs the upper lip.
ai.habitat: The Tonkin Huia Frog inhabits rocky, fast-flowing streams within dense evergreen forests at elevations ranging from 400 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Tonkin Huia Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a distinct defensive strategy by leaping into fast-flowing streams to escape predators when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Odorrana nasica* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, though specific clutch size data is currently limited.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Odorrana nasica* is found in Northeast India, specifically within the states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Tonkin Huia Frog emits a high-pitched, bird-like series of short, melodic whistles while perched on rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
